s1.syndrome_frame: Acute cardiac syndrome with respiratory distress and hemodynamic instability
salient_findings: Severe left ventricular dysfunction on echocardiography
key_facts: Patient presented with chest pain and dyspnea
Patient had symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior
Vital signs: temperature 36.5°C, heart rate 88 beats per minute, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, blood pressure 105/70 mm Hg, oxygen saturation 89% on room air
Patient lost consciousness 20 minutes after arrival
Blood pressure decreased to 67/43 mm Hg after loss of consciousness
Troponin T level: 4.74 μg/L
Pro-brain natriuretic peptide level: 4850 pg/mL
C-reactive protein level: 18.50 mg/L
Procalcitonin level: 39.68 ng/mL
Echocardiography showed severe left ventricular dysfunction with ejection fraction 38%
Coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries
ECG showed upward QRS complex in lead aVR and pure R wave in leads V1 and V2 initially
Follow-up ECG showed sinus tachycardia, low QRS voltage in limb leads, ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, aVF, and V1-V6, and ST-segment depression in leads aVR and aVL

shortlist.label: Myocarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T, pro-brain natriuretic peptide, and C-reactive protein levels, along with symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection and severe left ventricular dysfunction

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Severe left ventricular dysfunction, wall motion abnormalities, and hemodynamic instability, with normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Acute myocardial infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated troponin T level and ST-segment elevation on ECG, although coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Severe left ventricular dysfunction, wall motion abnormalities, and hemodynamic instability, with symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection and stress

shortlist.label: Myopericarditis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated C-reactive protein and procalcitonin levels, along with symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection and severe left ventricular dysfunction

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of upper respiratory tract infection 3 days prior, elevated troponin T level, and severe left ventricular dysfunction with ejection fraction 38% on echocardiography are consistent with myocarditis. The normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography also support this diagnosis, as myocarditis is not typically associated with coronary artery disease.

rejected.label: Acute myocardial infarction
rejected.why: Normal coronary arteries on coronary angiography make this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results are more consistent with an inflammatory process such as myocarditis

rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's echocardiography results showed severe left ventricular dysfunction, but not the typical apical ballooning pattern seen in Takotsubo cardiomyopathy

rejected.label: Myopericarditis
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms and laboratory results could be consistent with myopericarditis, the echocardiography results showing severe left ventricular dysfunction are more suggestive of myocarditis
